rv.q: The shock of the play, is its warmth, humour and gentle humanity.
Often deeply poignant but always hopeful, the presentation of a community at odds, still finding ways to come together proves, as The Revlon Girl herself insists, 'it's more than just lipstick.'
The Revlon Girl is a powerful piece of drama that respectfully touches on an event that wiped out a generation.

The Revlon Girl is a funny, poignant reminder that small pockets of joy can be found in the darkest of times, and that the greed of faceless corporations causes untold damage to everyday human beings.
The Revlon Girl is a short yet impressively evocative piece that handles the real-life source material with great care while generating such richly dynamic characters.

cn.t: Docking's play about Aberfan's grieving mothers balances brazen hilarity with brittle pathos, finding hope amid tragedy. Critics praise its poignant exploration of an untouchable subject brought joyously to life.
